scope: Platform-wide YouTube branded-content rules versus U.S. FTC endorsement guidance for U.S.-relevant consumers; not individualized legal advice

policy_layers.title: YouTube Studio and branded-content policy
policy_layers.creator_action: Declare covered paid promotion in the video's Studio branded-content control, and review product-category, geo and age policies
policy_layers.coverage: videos, Shorts, live, descriptions, comments and other features when branded

policy_layers.title: U.S. FTC Endorsement Guides and staff guidance
policy_layers.jurisdiction: United States; posts from abroad can be covered when impact on U.S. consumers is reasonably foreseeable
policy_layers.creator_action: Assess material connection and whether context needs a conspicuous in-content, understandable disclosure
policy_layers.coverage: sponsored and materially connected endorsements, including some noncash perks and affiliate links

policy_layers.title: Other national or regional requirements
policy_layers.creator_action: Research the actual countries and product categories involved before publication
policy_layers.coverage: Unknown without separate jurisdiction and campaign facts

relationship_cases.caveat: Individual sponsorship terms and audiovisual placement remain fact dependent

relationship_cases.connection: noncash benefit received in expectation of endorsement or otherwise materially relevant
relationship_cases.caveat: Tiny incidental gifts may be evaluated contextually; do not make an absolute legal rule for every unsolicited item

relationship_cases.connection: purchase through tracked referral may generate creator commission
relationship_cases.caveat: Affiliate labels, descriptions and platform commerce modules do not all have identical disclosure rules

relationship_cases.connection: creator endorses an owned business or product
relationship_cases.caveat: No generic assumption that promoting one's own product always requires the same disclaimer

relationship_cases.connection: no financial, familial, employment or brand material connection
relationship_cases.caveat: Actual relationships must be established; a video topic alone does not prove sponsorship

surface_guidance.us_guidance: In-content disclosure with the endorsement; descriptions alone are insufficient, and audiovisual formats should consider both audible and visible disclosure
Conspicuous disclosure visible or audible where endorsements occur, not a hidden or truncated description
Repeat disclosure periodically because audience members may arrive partway through
Clearly state commission/material connection near the recommendation and link; bare 'affiliate link' can be inadequate

dated_changes.description: U.S. FTC updated the Endorsement Guides including clarity and platform-tool concerns
TeamYouTube announced refreshed branded-content labels, age and geographic content controls, and planned automated declaration detection

safeguards: Platform declaration and independent legal obligations are separate gates; no button creates a universal legal safe harbor.
Never infer sponsorship from a channel's language, topic, age or viewer demographics.
Review product-category restrictions and age/geo limits before publishing. Do not assume the controls mean content is legal everywhere.
A September rollout announcement is not a verified global activation date or detection accuracy measurement.
FTC staff guidance is not a universal rule for all countries or a substitute for legal advice.
No individual sponsor contracts, creator identities, financial details or confidential campaign documents are collected.
